Hereditary transthyretin V30M amyloidosis (familial amyloid polyneuropathy) can involve the heart, causing restrictive cardiomyopathy, but echocardiography and ECG have certain features that can help differentiate amyloid cardiomyopathy from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Typically, echocardiography shows concentric thickening, sparkling appearance, small LV cavity, diastolic dysfunction, while HCM shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy, systolic anterior motion, etc. ECG in amyloidosis often shows low voltage despite thick walls, pseudo-infarction patterns. In HCM, voltage is often high. So these modalities can discriminate, though not perfectly; sometimes overlapping. So answer likely "yes". Confidence maybe 80. Provide JSON.
